summary: Oregon Department of Forestry lookout on Buxton Mountain: a 100-foot tower built 1941, replaced 1963, removed 1998. The register says only a foundation piece remains.

facts.design: 100-foot wooden L-6 tower (1941), replaced by a 99-foot timber tower with a 7x7 cab (1963)
facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1998; the register says only a foundation piece remains

events.note: Camp program plans a mile-long road to the summit and a 100-foot tower with cabin
Activated March 9, 1942, under the Portland Filter Center; a 1942 report plans observers and a fire guard for the season
Construction begins on the new 99-foot tower and lookout cabin
99-foot timber tower with a 7x7 cab completed (Rex's page says 9x9 cab)
Lookout Marcia Yeater spotted a smoke near Manning; the person who came on the radio admitted burning trash beside a house
Tower removed; staffed into the 1970s before removal

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Oregon Lookouts give a 7x7 cab; firelookout.com gives 9x9. The story uses 7x7 and notes the disagreement.
One 1940 entry in Oregon Lookouts gives 113 feet; the register, Rex's page and a 1942 entry give 100 feet. The story uses 100 feet.

notes_for_editor: The core timeline (1941 tower, 1963 replacement, 1998 removal) agrees across all three sources. Open points: the 7x7 vs 9x9 cab, the single 113-foot 1940 entry, and the 'today' description, which rests on the register's foundation-piece statement and a photo caption. One search found nothing newer. Access is not stated. Height 30.5 m matches the original 100-foot tower; the 1963 tower was 99 feet.
